None None
`SnapshotForTesting` doc overclaims concurrency safety, and it ships in the production binary

**Doc claim (registry.go:42-43):** "Both capture and restore hold registryMu, so it is safe against concurrent registry readers." True for readers. But restore does `registry = snapshot` — a wholesale replacement — so any `Register` that lands between capture and restore is silently discarded. It is not safe against concurrent *writers*, and the sentence reads as a general safety guarantee.

Benign today: every caller is a non-parallel test (they use `t.Setenv`/`t.Chdir`), Go does not run top-level parallel tests concurrently with serial ones, and `Register` almost always happens in `init`. Worth narrowing the sentence to what it guarantees, since the next caller will read it as blanket cover.

**Placement:** it lives in `registry.go`, so a testing-only helper is compiled into the shipped binary and exported to every importer of `agent`. It genuinely cannot go in `agent`'s `_test.go` — package `cli` needs it — but a dedicated `registry_testing.go`, or a small `agenttest` subpackage, would keep the intent legible at the call site. Noting the tradeoff was made rather than claiming it is wrong.

The helper itself is the right fix for a real problem, and the doc explains that problem well (temp-dir binaries leaking into the process-global registry so `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` execs deleted files). `TestSnapshotForTesting_RestoresRegistry` covers it.

```
    opencode
    pi
    roger-roger    <- external plugin
    zed            <- external plugin
```

`roger-roger` and `zed` render identically to `claude-code`. That defeats the flag's purpose — a user passes `--external` precisely to see what discovery found on their PATH — and the distinction is trust-relevant, since external agents are arbitrary executables resolved from `$PATH` rather than code shipped in the binary.

A `(external)` suffix, or a second section under the built-ins, would make the superset legible. `external.IsExternal(ag)` is already computed one line above at `agent_group.go:98`, so the information is in hand.

This is a consequence of the superset change rather than a pre-existing gap: under the earlier "instead of" semantics the mode itself told you which list you were looking at.

Three problems, in descending order of relevance to this PR:

**1. `zed` is absent.** Named discovery only resolves the name the user typed, so on the typo path nothing external is registered by the time `printAgentError` (`setup.go:1833-1846`) reads `agent.List()`. The user whose external plugin this PR just made addable gets an "Available agents" list that omits it — exactly the confusion #1928 was filed about, one keystroke away. The error path is the natural place to pay for a full scan, since it only runs when the command already failed: `external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx)` before printing, or at minimum a line pointing at `entire agent list --external`.

**2. `vogon` (test-only) is listed.** `printAgentError` uses `agent.List()`, which does not filter `agent.TestOnly`; the new `runAgentList` does filter it (`agent_group.go:93-95`). Same command surface, two different answers to "what agents are available".

**3. Wrong usage line.** "Usage: entire enable --agent <agent-name>" when reached from `entire agent add`.

2 and 3 are pre-existing, but 2 is a direct inconsistency with the filtering this PR just added, and 3 gets more visible as `agent add` becomes the promoted path.

## Summary
`entire agent add/list/remove` omitted external agents (e.g. `zed`), failing with `Unknown agent`, even though `entire enable --agent <name>` and the git-hook paths worked. The `agent` noun-group never invoked external-agent discovery, so `agent.Get` / `agent.List` only saw statically-registered built-ins.

Fixes #1928.

## Changes
- `add` / `remove` `RunE`: resolve the single named plugin via `external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, name)` before `agent.Get` / `runRemoveAgent`. Targeting the exact name (rather than a full `$PATH` scan) avoids executing every unrelated `entire-agent-*` binary, and surfaces a real plugin load error instead of a generic "unknown agent". Built-in names short-circuit instantly (no exec); an unknown name still falls through to `printWrongAgentError`. These bypass the `external_agents` gate because the action is itself the opt-in — and `add` auto-persists `external_agents=true` for an external agent (via `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`).
- `entire agent list`: **default lists built-in agents only** — no `$PATH` scan and no plugin exec, so the listing stays fast regardless of how many `entire-agent-*` binaries are on `$PATH`. A footer points at `--external`.
- **`--external`** lists external agent plugins on `$PATH` (installed and available) via full discovery, reusing the built-in rendering — same `Agents:` header, installed `✓` marker, and test-only filter — so output is uniform.
  - This replaces the earlier `--all` flag. Previously the default path executed every plugin on `$PATH` to mark installed externals — a per-plugin exec cost that scaled with plugin count on a sub-100ms command. All external work is now behind the explicit `--external` opt-in.
- Discovery lives in the run function (not the group's `PersistentPreRunE`), so unit tests calling `runAgentList` directly exercise it.

## Test
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagListsAvailablePlugin`: the default listing does not scan `$PATH` (an available external plugin is absent); `--external` lists it.
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagMarksInstalled`: `--external` lists an installed external plugin marked `✓`.
- Both use an isolated repo and a `#!/bin/sh` mock plugin on `$PATH`; skip when no POSIX shell is available.

## Verification
- `mise run fmt` — clean
- `mise run lint` (golangci-lint 2.11.3) — 0 issues (cli + external pkgs)
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/ -run 'AgentList|AgentGroup|ExternalAgent'` — PASS
- Benchmark (9 shell plugins on `$PATH`, `external_agents:true`): default `agent list` **18 execs → 0**; external listing moved behind `--external`. Full `mise run test:ci` not yet run.
